Lemi Orhan Ergin

Software crafter. Co-founder of Craftgate.

I have been writing code since 2001, in technical leadership and coaching roles at Sony, eBay/GittiGidiyor, ACM and iyzico. Today I build Craftgate, a payment orchestration platform, as its Chief Software Crafter. I founded the Software Craftsmanship Turkey community in 2014, and I talk about how good software gets made: craftsmanship, team culture, and what is still worth keeping now that code is cheap to generate.

Git is a graph

git log --graph --all

In 2016 I gave a talk in Turkish, Git: Not What You Think. Its one idea: every git command is a move on a graph. Commits are nodes; branches, tags and HEAD are pointers to them. Here you run real git commands, typed or tapped together, and move commits and pointers until your graph matches the goal. Each level is a piece of my own history, and solving it tells you a little more about me.

The game runs in your browser with JavaScript, which is off here. These are its levels.

  1. Hello, 2001 Make two commits on main. Watch what the main pointer does.
  2. Pointers, not copies Create a branch called sony, switch to it, and commit on it. main must stay where it is.
  3. I left twice Merge air-force back into main so the detour stays visible. A fast-forward would hide it.
  4. Launch day Tag the commit "Public launch" as launch. Do not move any branch.
  5. Forgot something Fix the last commit instead of adding a new one.
  6. Straight lines Move typofix on top of main without a merge commit.
  7. Only what is tested Bring only the two tested commits from experiments onto main, in their original order.
  8. We pursued neither Move main back two commits, as if those calls never happened. Nobody else has seen them yet.
  9. Undo in public main is public. Undo the commit "Credential check" without rewriting history.
  10. Nothing is lost Bring the branch scturkey back exactly where it was, and stay on main. git reflog remembers where HEAD has been.
  11. Burning the ships Move craftgate's own two commits off services and directly onto main. Leave services where it is.
  12. Ship the talk Put talk on top of main, merge it into main with a merge commit, tag that merge devoxx, and delete the talk branch.
